provenance.temporal_biology_evidence: The 2024 kelp paper associates ocean-modelled dispersal with biomass synchrony after accounting for geographic distance, nitrate and waves; it does not experimentally establish that the same network loses colonization insurance from joint source failure.
provenance.biological_data_source: LTER 1996-2006 kelp semiannual patch series, exact versions and compatibility unverified

ecological_tension: Overlapping geographic source influence does not imply demographic insurance when source populations fail synchronously.

I_independent_insurance.mechanism: When sources fluctuate independently, multiple sources accessing one target buffer poor propagule production by a single source.
I_independent_insurance.prediction: At fixed expected target propagule supply and habitat, increased independently varying effective source count predicts lower probability of no future source supply and higher future colonization/persistence.

II_synchrony_erodes_insurance.mechanism: Positive covariance of fluctuations among accessible source populations concentrates shared failure risk, reducing temporal insurance even when static graph-access contributions are balanced.
II_synchrony_erodes_insurance.prediction: At fixed source count, average access, expected propagule output, spatial opportunity and local conditions, stronger preceding-source synchrony predicts more joint poor-source-production episodes and poorer subsequent recolonization; total source count may have no protective slope.

III_local_habitat_and_common_shock.mechanism: Wave climate, nutrient stress and local habitat synchronize sources and targets; dispersal is not the unique cause.
III_local_habitat_and_common_shock.prediction: The apparent synchrony-insurance increment disappears after shared environmental shocks and local habitat are controlled without future leakage.

separated_endpoints.colonization: For targets unoccupied at t, measured patch arrival/occupancy at t+1 with observation support
separated_endpoints.persistence: For targets occupied at t, continuing patch presence at t+1 with separate risk set
separated_endpoints.joint_source_failure: Multiple lagged source patches show concurrently low viable spore production, relative to prespecified historical source baseline
separated_endpoints.regional_risk: Population-level synchrony and regional variability, not automatic inference of regional extinction probability

preoutcome_constraints.matched_null_reason: A valid covariance null needs to preserve both geography and shared shocks while selectively disrupting residual dependence. This is unresolved and therefore no randomization or score is authorized.

proposed_test_order: If exact source-to-target physical transport and patch-time identities cannot be verified, terminal STOP.
If local habitats and years do not provide independent turnover events or source production measured before target outcomes, terminal NONESTIMABLE.
Freeze data-independent source-neighbourhood and environmental covariates, then evaluate directed lagged source supply and prespecified earlier-window source covariance without target leakage.
Use separate and adequately powered 0->1 and 1->0 transition endpoints and hold out later periods and independent spatial groupings.

Treat published kelp source as design/outcome-context-exposed retrospective benchmark. Pristine confirmatory inference still requires a genuinely independent lineage with Structural v0.31/v0.42 admission.

novelty_boundary.known: Dispersal and environmental conditions influence kelp synchrony (Wanner et al. 2024); connectivity contributes to kelp demography (Castorani et al. 2015, 2017).
novelty_boundary.proposed_increment: Whether *overlapping source access* creates temporal demographic insurance depends on residual correlation of actual source failures, and whether that correlation predicts later target recolonization or persistence beyond expected propagule supply and shared disturbances.
